summary: An excerpt from a novel ("Book 15 — part 110") in which Ray Marlowe meets Amah, an imposing elderly woman weaving a plaited bark basket, in a room with Emma. Amah sharply criticizes Ray's manners and assumptions, citing the family's recent troubles, including Micah and Emma and Frederick's mother, and challenges him on whether he knows the Whiston family's affairs. Emma pleads with Amah, and the exchange turns on the difference between perception and truth and what courtesy requires.
one_line: Ray Marlowe is rebuked by the formidable elderly Amah, a basket weaver, over manners and his grasp of the Whiston family's troubles.
key_facts: The woman Ray meets is called Amah, and her voice is described as rich and deep, projected like a roll of thunder.
Amah is weaving a basket from thin strips of plaited bark, spread across her wide thighs as a broad, dun colored disk.
Amah tells Ray, "You look, but you don't gawk, Mr. Marlowe," and says these are better manners than he has shown toward the family so far.
Amah asks Ray whether he is a fool, saying the affairs of the Whiston family are beyond his ken.
Emma says, "Amah, this is Ray," and later reminds Amah, "Amah, you promised."
Amah lists the family's recent trials as "First Emma and Frederick's mother, then Micah, and now here you are, a distraction at best."
Amah accuses Ray of manhandling Frederick after Frederick let his temper get the better of him.
Amah refers to Ray compromising the virtue of a young woman in the middle of the night when he thought no one was watching.
Ray says "I'm sorry" reflexively, and Amah asks him for what reason he is apologizing.
Ray tells Amah, "I had no intention of causing difficulties for you," and she replies that intentions and actual consequences do not necessarily correspond.
Amah says Ray has been apprised of the current situation, and when he says he realizes the timing is unfortunate, she asks, "Do you?"
Amah states that "The ability to separate truth from fiction is the foundation of courtesy."
Ray responds to Amah's lecture by repeating the word "Courtesy?" and the excerpt ends mid-sentence as he speaks it.
Emma shifts nervously from one foot to the other beside Ray during the confrontation.
